title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'loop equation' [α,β] = ρ in G = GL(M) or SL(M), with M a rank-2 projective module over a base S (ultimately S = Spec Z). This is the relation in the fundamental group of a once-punctured torus, where the loop around the puncture equals the commutator of the two generating loops. On the previous page, ρ is assumed regular: on every fibre it generates a rank-2 subalgebra. Then A_ρ = O_S + O_S ρ is a quadratic algebra that is locally a direct summand of End(M). Its unit scheme T_ρ is the Weil restriction R_{A_ρ/O_S} G_m, and T_ρ is the centralizer of ρ in GL(M).

This page proceeds as follows.
(1) ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has characteristic polynomial x²−x+1, discriminant −3 and order 6. In characteristic 3 the polynomial becomes (x+1)², so ρ is not semisimple there. The fibre of A_ρ at 3 is F_3[x]/(x+1)², whose unit group is G_m × G_a. So T_ρ = R_{Z[ζ6]/Z} G_m is a torus away from 3, and at 3 it is the product of a G_m with a unipotent group.
(2) Likewise σ = σ_∞ = [[0,−1],[1,0]] has σ⁴ = 1 and σ² = −1, characteristic polynomial x²+1 and discriminant −4. It is semisimple outside characteristic 2 and unipotent in characteristic 2, since (σ+1)² = 2σ. So T_σ = R_{Z[i]/Z} G_m is a torus except at 2, where it is G_m times a unipotent group.
(3) Back to the general case. The centralizer of ρ in SL(M) is ST_ρ = Ker(N: T_ρ → G_m), the norm-one torus, since the determinant restricted to A_ρ is the norm.
(4) Key observation. T_ρ-torsors are Zariski-locally trivial: by Shapiro and Hilbert 90, H¹(S, R_{A_ρ/S} G_m) = Pic(A_ρ). This fails for ST_ρ. The sequence A_ρ^* → O_S^* → H¹(S, ST_ρ) → Pic(A_ρ) shows an extra obstruction O_S^*/N(A_ρ^*), and units of a local ring need not be norms.
(5) Application to the equation. For given ξ, the equation [α,ρ] = ξ means α ρ α⁻¹ = ξρ. The solutions α form a torsor under the centralizer as soon as ξρ is locally conjugate to ρ, which is guaranteed by the proposition's conditions det ξ = 1 and Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ. So [α,β] = ρ is solvable Zariski-locally in GL(M), but perhaps not in SL(M).

The next page specializes to S = Spec Z. There the obstruction is an invertible A_ρ-module, which vanishes because Pic(Z[ζ6]) = 1.
errors: Equation number (13) is used twice: once for σ, once for the centralizers. A minor slip.
The machine transcription's 'δT_ρ' is almost certainly 'ST_ρ', the special (norm-one) centralizer.
No mathematical errors detected. The fibre claims at 3 and at 2, and the torsor triviality claims, are correct.

ideas.what: The centralizer of a regular element ρ of GL(M) over a base is the unit group of the quadratic algebra O_S[ρ], i.e. a Weil restriction of G_m. It is a torus exactly where ρ is fibrewise semisimple, and degenerates to G_m × G_a at primes dividing the discriminant (3 for order 6, 2 for order 4).
ideas.modern_name: Centralizers of regular elements / Weil restriction tori over Z with bad fibres
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (SGA3-style group schemes; Steinberg, Kostant for regular elements)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of SGA3; not this specific example

ideas.what: Torsors under R_{A/S} G_m are Zariski-locally trivial (Hilbert 90 / Shapiro), whereas torsors under the norm-one torus are not. Consequently the conjugacy equation αρα⁻¹ = ξρ is Zariski-locally solvable in GL but possibly not in SL.
ideas.modern_name: Hilbert 90 for Weil restrictions; norm-one torus cohomology; rational vs stable conjugacy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hilbert, Serre's Cohomologie galoisienne; Langlands/Kottwitz for stable conjugacy)
ideas.where_published: Hilbert 90 in Grothendieck's descent formalism (SGA1/FGA), not in this form

ideas.what: Solving the once-punctured-torus loop relation [α,β] = ρ scheme-theoretically over Spec Z with boundary monodromy of finite order (6 or 4, i.e. the elliptic points of SL2(Z)).
ideas.modern_name: Relative character varieties of the once-punctured torus; integral points on Markov-type surfaces x²+y²+z²−xyz−2 = tr ρ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fricke–Klein (trace identities); Goldman; integral-points work by Ghosh–Sarnak, Whang
ideas.where_published: Related only loosely to La Longue Marche / Esquisse (Teichmüller tower, genus-1 one-puncture)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly separates the GL-version from the SL-version of the loop equation [α,β] = ρ over a general base. The SL obstruction is the class of a norm-one torus torsor, not just Pic(A_ρ). This is an integral, scheme-theoretic treatment of the relative character variety of the once-punctured torus at elliptic boundary monodromy, which is mildly unusual. The mathematics itself is standard.
missed.quote: c'est possible (loc. Zar.) dans G(M), mais peut-être pas dans SG(M).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It touches integral-points questions for Markov-type cubic surfaces and arithmetic of SL2 commutator equations. The page adds no new result, though.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard computation: centralizers as Weil-restriction tori with bad fibres at 3 and 2, plus Hilbert 90 versus norm-one torsors. It is set in Grothendieck's unusual integral framing of the loop equation, but nothing here would surprise a specialist.
